national.note: AHR 2025 (from a snippet): violations per community water system fell 11%, from 2.8 (2023) to 2.5 (2024); the state range runs from 0 (Hawaii) to 5.5 (state not named).

alternates.measure: share of CWS-served population on systems with a health-based violation
alternates.note: EPA: 92.4% served by systems with no health-based violation in FY2023, so 7.6% served by systems with one. Separately, surface water treatment rule violations affected 14.4 million people (4.5%).

alternates.measure: share of public water systems with a health-based violation
alternates.note: 6,045 of 148,541 active public water systems in 2023 (snippet).

conflicts: No state-level cross-check was possible: every primary host (americashealthrankings.org, its assets host, epa.gov, echo.epa.gov, newsweek.com, visualcapitalist.com, wikipedia.org) returned EGRESS_BLOCKED, and search snippets did not carry per-state values.
Measure (a) is no longer published by AHR. The current AHR measure (hb_water_violation) is violations per community water system, not the share of population served.

State violation counts found in the media (Visual Capitalist 2023: PA 24,525, TX 15,340, WV 7,473; Newsweek: PA 8,083, NJ 7,371, CA 7,054, NY 6,743, OK 5,188, AK 4,715, MI 4,551, IL 4,469, HI 2) count ALL SDWA violation types, including monitoring and reporting, not health-based violations only. They do not fit measure (b) and were not used.

Some third-party snippets gave Alabama '22.8% of utilities with violations (2023)' and Oklahoma '4% of public water systems with a health-based violation'. They are unverified and outside the measure, and were not used.
